bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/keychain.rs (generic secrets only), springboard/src/bare/account.rs (local OS account), springboard/src/shell/login.rs (sign-in), bifrost-cloud account API (separate repo)
summary: Apple's Accounts framework is deprecated (landing page: for new apps, use the service provider's SDK). BifrOSt has no system account store, no account types, no OAuth credential objects and no access-grant prompt for third-party accounts. The closest pieces are a per-app keychain for opaque secrets and the local OS account used for desktop sign-in.

features.apple: ACAccountStore: accounts, account(withIdentifier:), accounts(with:), saveAccount, removeAccount, requestAccessToAccounts
features.note: No SDK object that lists or saves the user's accounts across apps.

features.apple: ACAccount: identifier, username, userFullName, accountDescription, accountType, credential
features.bifrost: springboard/src/bare/account.rs (Account: local OS account from /var/lib/springboard/account and passwd)
features.note: The OS knows the local user name, uid, gid and home. No app-facing SDK API exposes it, and it is not a registry of third-party accounts.

features.bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/keychain.rs (add, get, update, delete of opaque bytes by service and account)
features.note: An app can store a token itself as an opaque secret. There is no typed credential, no refresh token or expiry field, and no shared store between apps.
The manifest permission binds only keychain access. There is no account-type registry and no user prompt that grants access to a type of account.
No token refresh path. Apps refresh tokens themselves through springboard/sdk/src/url.rs (URLSession) if needed.

features.apple: Account sign-in sheets and the 'create account in app' flow of requestAccessToAccounts
features.bifrost: springboard/src/shell/login.rs (desktop sign-in: password field, authentication through privd, lockout)
features.note: Desktop login only. There is no sheet an app can present to add a third-party account.

features.feature: Secure secret storage used for credentials
features.apple: Keychain items as the backing store of account credentials (Accounts keeps them in its database)
features.note: Per-app, encrypted with a master key on the same disk. No access groups, so apps cannot share credentials, and no user-presence protection.

features.apple: Not part of Accounts; Apple's equivalent is Apple Account sign-in
features.note: The cloud account lives on the server and is not exposed to apps through an SDK API in bifrost-os.

features.bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/keychain.rs (keychain Error codes that mirror Security OSStatus values)
features.note: No Accounts error domain. Keychain errors are mirrored from Apple's Security codes, not from Accounts.

gaps: No system account store (ACAccountStore): no list, save, remove or lookup of user accounts that apps share.
No account type registry and no access-grant prompt (requestAccessToAccounts, accessGranted).
No typed OAuth credential objects, token expiry or credential renewal.
No SDK API for the local OS account (bare/account.rs) or for the BifrOSt cloud account.
The framework itself is deprecated by Apple; new apps should use the service provider's SDK, so parity here is low priority.
